notes.meaning: True wisdom is rare and makes a person stand out. It gives someone the insight to explain hard questions and understand God's ways. Wisdom also changes how a person looks, softening a stern, proud face into one of gentleness and peace.

Subjects are urged to obey the lawful commands of their ruler. This duty is not just about keeping civil peace; it also honors the solemn oath made before God to submit to authority. Honoring God includes keeping the promises we make in His name.

A wise servant does not storm out of the king's presence in anger or take part in a rebellion. Earthly rulers hold great power and can act as they please. It is foolish to persist in an offense when the ruler has the power to punish it.

A king's royal decree carries supreme authority in his realm. Ordinary people cannot easily challenge him or ask what he is doing. Recognizing lawful power keeps citizens humble and careful in their conduct.

Those who follow rightful orders stay out of trouble with the governing authorities. A wise person has the good sense to know the proper time and the best way to act or speak. Discretion helps avoid unnecessary conflict.

There is a fitting time and proper method for everything that needs to be done. Yet human misery is heavy because people often fail to recognize that right time. Acting foolishly or out of turn brings unnecessary trouble upon oneself.

No human being knows the future, nor can any person tell someone else what tomorrow holds. This lack of knowledge often makes people anxious and troubled. Since our days are uncertain, we must lean entirely on God's guidance.

No one has the power to hold back the wind or keep the breath of life in the body when death arrives. Just as soldiers cannot leave the front lines during battle, no one can escape the final struggle of death. In the end, evil schemes will never rescue the wicked from their judgment.

The Teacher carefully examined everything that happens in this earthly life. He saw that power is frequently abused when one person rules over another. Oppression harms the subjects, but it also brings destruction and judgment upon the tyrant himself.

Wicked rulers who visited sacred places often receive lavish, honorable funerals when they die. In contrast, upright people who lived godly lives are sometimes quickly driven out and forgotten in the city. This topsy-turvy outcome is another example of life's painful unfairness under the sun.

other.label: Catholic
other.view: Following the Latin translation, some older Catholic teachers understood this verse as describing hypocrites who disguise their evil in the church and receive empty human praise.

notes.meaning: When wrongdoers are not punished right away, other people become bold and eager to commit evil. They mistake God's patience for indifference or approval. While God delays judgment to give time for repentance, justice is never forgotten.

A sinner may commit crime after crime and still seem to live a long, comfortable life. Despite this apparent injustice, the Teacher firmly holds that true good belongs only to those who revere God. Faith trusts that God will reward those who honor Him in their hearts.

It will never truly go well for those who reject God. Even if their earthly lives seem long, their days are fleeting and empty like a passing shadow. Because they do not fear the Lord, their end will be ruined.

Another puzzling frustration on earth is that good people often suffer the kind of troubles that wicked people deserve. At the same time, evil people frequently receive the rewards and blessings that righteous people should enjoy. From a purely human point of view, this seems completely unfair and futile.

Because life has so many mysteries, the Teacher advises people to enjoy simple everyday blessings. There is nothing better under the sun than eating, drinking, and finding wholesome joy in one's honest work. This peace of mind is God's gracious gift to sustain us through our brief earthly labors.

The Teacher set his heart to study wisdom and observe all the hard labor people carry out on earth. He saw people working so relentlessly that they lost sleep night and day. Yet all that restless striving cannot unlock life's deepest secrets.

No matter how hard people work, no human being can fully understand everything God does in the world. Even the wisest scholars cannot discover the full meaning of His providence. Instead of wearing ourselves out trying to solve every riddle, we are called to trust God and rest in His care.
